title: California Capitol Hosts First Diwali Celebration on Its West Steps
excerpt: Assemblymembers Ash Kalra and Darshana Patel co-hosted the November 5 celebration with the Association of Indo Americans, days before California's first official Diwali state holiday.
body:
• The California State Capitol hosted a Diwali celebration on its West Steps for the first time on Thursday, November 5, 2026, from 2:00 to 5:00 p.m.
  • Assemblymembers Ash Kalra and Dr. Darshana Patel co-hosted the free community event with the Association of Indo Americans and the Federation of Indian Associations of San Diego.
  • India's Consul General in San Francisco, Satish Kumar Sivan, attended; the programme included cultural performances, a ceremonial diya lighting and Indian snacks, and the Capitol was illuminated in Diwali colours as evening approached.
  • The celebration came days before California's first official Diwali state holiday — Diwali fell on Sunday, November 8, 2026, under the 2025 law AB 268.

The California State Capitol hosted a Diwali celebration on its West Steps for the first time on Thursday, November 5, bringing state legislators, Indian American community leaders, cultural organisations and families to Sacramento for the Festival of Lights, according to hi INDiA's report of the event.

Who Hosted It

The celebration was co-hosted by the Association of Indo Americans (AIA), Assemblymembers Ash Kalra and Dr. Darshana Patel, the Federation of Indian Associations (FIA) of San Diego and other community organisations. Satish Kumar Sivan, Consul General of India in San Francisco, attended alongside Assemblymembers and other guests. The free community event ran from 2:00 to 5:00 p.m. on the West Steps, at 10th Street and Capitol Mall, according to the event's Eventbrite listing.

Performances, Diyas and a Lit-Up Capitol

The programme featured Indian cultural performances, a ceremonial diya lighting and Indian snacks, with a traditional Diwali display and decorations provided by BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha. As evening approached, the Capitol building was illuminated in Diwali colours. Participants travelled from across California — including the San Francisco Bay Area and Silicon Valley, San Diego, Sacramento and Stockton — and some attendees came from neighbouring Nevada, hi INDiA reported.

"We can proudly say that we were part of history — the very first Diwali celebration on the West Steps of the California State Capitol."

— An attendee, quoted by hi INDiA

Days Before California's First Diwali Holiday

The timing gave the celebration an added marker. In 2025, the California Legislature recognised Diwali as an official state holiday through AB 268, and this year's festival fell on Sunday, November 8, 2026, according to the Assembly's House Resolution 137 marking the festival. AIA members described the West Steps event as a milestone in recognising Indian heritage and California's cultural diversity, and the association thanked the co-hosting lawmakers, the Consul General, performers and volunteers.

Diwali celebrations have been held inside the Capitol building before — BAPS organised one in 2019 — but organisers and attendees framed this year's gathering as the first held on the West Steps, the building's public front. For California's Indian American community, the sequence mattered: a community celebration on the Capitol steps in the same week the festival took its place on the state's official holiday calendar.
